title: Auburn's annual Parade of Lights has new route, Christmas movie theme - NewsBreak
text:
By Jon Becker ,
2 hours ago Auburn's annual Parade of Lights took place along Midland Street in 2022. The parade featured illuminated vehicles, floats and people. This year's Parade of Lights is on Saturday, Dec. 6. (Victoria Ritter/Midland Daily News) The season’s first snowfall may have quickly melted away, but the Auburn community’s energy and enthusiasm for the holiday season continue with its ninth annual Parade of Lights on Saturday, Dec. 6.
This year’s theme is Christmas Movie Magic, and event organizers have a suggestion for businesses and organizations that plan to have a float in this year’s parade: decorate it to reflect your favorite Christmas movie. The favorites are plentiful, be it National Lampoon’s Christmas Vacation, It’s a Wonderful Life, How the Grinch Stole Christmas, A Christmas Story, Home Alone, or Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer, to name but a few classics.
If you want to spark debate, have your float or lighted vehicle portray Die Hard, starring Bruce Willis. Some say it qualifies as a Christmas movie, while others beg to differ. Wherever you stand on the Die Hard Christmas debate, you’ll want to be standing on Midland Road on parade night as floats make their way from Bay Western High School and Middle School east to Auburn Elementary, a distance of just under a mile.
“It’s when Christ came into the world,” said Lee Kilbourn, a longtime Auburn businessman and the town’s former mayor. “It’s a joyful, wonderful time of year. Our parade just has a special effect on people. It gets people out and offers us a chance to wish our neighbors well and share in the magic of the season.”
Kilbourn said this year’s parade route has changed a bit from years past.
“The new, simpler parade route has no turns,” he said. “It’s a straight shot down Midland Road and we’ll have two or three cookie and hot cocoa stations along the way. Rogers Family Foods here will be donating 500 cookies and Iron Grind will be open for treats as well. It’s a special, festive evening in Auburn.”
Santa Claus will be part of the parade and will circle back from its conclusion at Auburn Elementary to Machelski Park at the corner of Nine Mile and Midland roads, where he will greet youngsters and be available for photographs.
Presented by the Auburn Area Chamber of Commerce and the Auburn-Williams Lions Club, the Parade of Lights begins at 6 p.m. and will also include a lighting of the town’s Christmas tree. The Chamber is accepting float donations so it can Adopt-A-Family and help brighten their holiday season.
The Chamber is also awarding prizes in three float categories at 5:30 p.m. prior to the start of the parade: Most Lit, Most Christmas Cheer and Judges’ Favorite.
If you’re interested in being in the parade, visit the Auburn Area Chamber of Commerce Facebook page.
